findings.reason: The protected implementation is a clear, conventional iterative postorder solution at an expert-interview standard. `children`, `order`, `stack`, `subtree_sum`, and `retained` name the complete tree state precisely; the two-pass traversal avoids recursion-depth risk; and the recurrence is visible without unnecessary helpers or mutation of either input array. No material clarity, correctness, or complexity improvement warrants a candidate.

Reversing the recorded root-first traversal evaluates every child before its parent. At each node, adding every child's complete subtree sum produces exactly the original subtree sum, while adding every child's already-filtered retained count excludes descendants deleted lower in the tree. A zero total sets the whole subtree's retained count to zero; its sum remains zero when propagated, so deleting it cannot alter an ancestor's original sum. Induction over postorder proves retained[0] is the requested count.

An independent recursive oracle returned each original subtree sum together with a retained count that becomes zero at zero-sum roots. It, the protected app source, the immutable native source, an independent leaf-queue aggregation, and a recompute-every-subtree control agreed on all ten visible cases, all three benchmark tiers, 31,764 exhaustive labeled trees, and 10,000 deterministic random valid trees. Inputs remained unchanged.

Exhaustive validation covered every valid tree rooted at 0 through five labeled nodes with every value vector over {-1,0,1}. The seeded random corpus included 9,604 trees with at least one later-indexed parent, 222 zero-sum roots, 7,904 zero-valued leaves, 6,993 zero-sum internal subtrees, and 9,863 trees containing a negative value. Separate legal 10,000-node chain and star checks covered maximum depth, width, and cardinality.

The unchanged hidden tiers use chain sizes n = 256, 1,024, and 4,096, a 16x span, with all-one values so every node remains. Across three real-test runs, the protected source passed at extra-growth exponents -0.01 through -0.00 and the independent linear leaf-queue control passed at -0.02 through +0.01. A correct control that materializes every subtree's complete member list returned every expected result and failed only scaling in five of five runs at +0.19 through +0.21. A Python-level recomputation control correctly hit the execution safety cap before scaling and was not used as verdict evidence. No benchmark edit was warranted.

The two authenticated source examples remain first and exact; the invented zero-root example remains correctly classified as a trial. Four hidden real rows were converted to visible trials without changing their inputs or expected outputs, and a visible later-indexed-parent case was added with both -10^5 and 10^5. All ten ordinary fixtures are now visible samples or trials and cover zero and nonzero singletons, zero leaves, internal and root cancellation, nested deletion, no deletion, negative nonzero sums, forward parent references, and both value limits.

Metadata consistently identifies Premium LeetCode algorithm problem 1273, Python as the app language, and Solution.deleteTreeNodes as the verified native entrypoint. Fresh authenticated evidence confirms the tree rooted at node 0, nodes/value/parent meanings, deletion of every zero-sum subtree, remaining-node count, node bound 1 through 10^4, matching array lengths, parent and value bounds, root sentinel -1, and valid-tree guarantee.

The protected app and immutable Accepted native sources have identical child-list construction, iterative traversal order, postorder reversal, subtree-sum and retained-count recurrence, zero-sum deletion, and root return; their only structural difference is the required app function versus LeetCode class-method wrapper and native typing import. submission.json remains bound to verified submission 2068268130, and both sources and the manifest remain unchanged.

The complete Approach matches the protected implementation exactly. It derives the iterative postorder construction, explains why deleted zero-sum children still propagate the correct numerical sum, proves the retained-count recurrence from leaves to root, states exact O(n) time and space, and discusses recursion depth, both principal quadratic alternatives, zero leaves and roots, nested deletion, and negative values.

The modular Reference preserves the three-part array representation, root identity, subtree-removal rule, requested remaining-node count, both authenticated examples in source order, all seven constraints, and all three source hints. It also makes explicit that the written contract does not impose parent-before-child index order.

A fresh authenticated Premium review confirmed two examples without explanations, seven constraints, three hints, and no source tables, images, diagrams, notes, or follow-up. source_fidelity.json binds all five modular Reference files to live-content SHA-256 fb909451f8c4d4dfbb001795e5ec21a98c0132fc482e721ce54879b9f7db4fda and validates without errors.
